It is -16% over 20 sessions, but almost flat since Nov 4 while IWM fell about 5%. The company-specific leg was Oct 14 to Nov 2, $20.6 to $16.5, with IWM up, and included -7% on Nov 2, the day the 6-K on the CFO's resignation was filed. No usable option chain (ATM spread 192% of mid). 20-day realised volatility is 74%, so one day of noise is about 4.7%. Prior reactions: Q1 (Jun 10) -8%, with the preliminary figures already out on May 14 and a large EPS miss; Q2 (Aug 18) +12.4%, on in-line revenue, a raised FY guide, a new FY27 guide of $400M+ and a 'record July $20.9M'. view: The Q3 revenue figure itself is not the news. Management set the guide in mid-August with July in hand, and it has landed inside its quarterly ranges before (Q2 $46.5M against a $46-48M guide). Three things in the release decide the reaction. The first is whatever monthly 'record' it names; this company discloses a record month with every print (Dec $10.0M, May $16.7M, July $20.9M). The second is whether the FY26 $220-230M guide holds, which needs a steep Q4 step-up to about $25M+ a month. The third is how bad the adjusted EBITDA loss is. Two pieces of evidence pull in opposite directions. Against momentum: boilerplate on Nov 3 and Nov 5 still quoted July's $251M run-rate, so no month through September beat July. US Google search interest for 'IM8' averaged about 74 in October, against about 92 in September and about 86 in July. And the group CFO resigned on Oct 30, 'to pursue new opportunities'. For the guide: the Nov 5 Care Bears release restated the FY26 $220-230M guide and said guidance reflects 'management's current estimates and assumptions as of the date of this press release'. That was written after October had closed. The same release's footnote says quarterly subscription plans are recognised in full on shipment, and 93% of revenue is subscription. So revenue clusters in renewal months (Oct 2025 was a record, 32% over September; July 2026 was a record). October 2026 is the next renewal month after July's record cohort, which makes an October record likely. My central case: Q3 in line at about $63M, a headline October record, and FY26 kept or narrowed toward the low end. That is mildly better than the most skeptical consensus, and the stock has de-rated 24% and is cheap on run-rate. Against that: an EBITDA loss still near -$19M a quarter, 'positive adjusted FCF' that counts General Catalyst facility draws, a weak small-cap and consumer-health tape (HIMS -40% in a month after its print), and a possible narrowing of the FY guide that consensus at $224M would read as a miss. Net, a slight lean up, nowhere near conviction.
unpriced: Possibly the mechanics of quarterly-subscription revenue recognition. An October renewal-month record is likely given July's cohort, and the Nov 5 'as of the date of this press release' restatement of FY guidance came with October already known. The Nov 2 sell-off on the CFO news and the run-rate stuck at $251M read as slowing momentum. But the evidence is indirect, the consensus figure is disputed ($211.8M against $224.3M), and I cannot show the price misses it by enough to act.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the FY26 guide and the October run-rate, not Q3 revenue, which management guided with half the quarter visible. The company restated the FY guide 'as of the date of' its Nov 5 release with October closed, and its quarterly-plan revenue recognition favours an October renewal-month record. Both lean up. But search interest has faded since September, the CFO resigned on Oct 30, the release will show losses that are still large, and the tape is risk-off, so I cannot get to 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A cut or narrowing of the FY26 $220-230M guide to its low end or below, or an October figure that is not a record above July's $20.9M, would make this a down print, likely by double digits.

self_critique: The up-lean rests on inference: renewal-month mechanics and a boilerplate 'as of' guidance line. Neither shows October's size, and the guide needs about $25M+ a month in Q4 against a flat Q3. A CFO resigning two and a half weeks before a print, and search interest down about 20% from September, are the kind of soft traces that precede a guide trim. A narrowing to the $220M low end would read as a miss against the $224M consensus. In a risk-off tape, a retail-heavy small cap losing about $19M a quarter can fall on an in-line print, as Q1's -8% did. That case is why I stay close to 50 and do not recommend.
approach_notes: Two parts of the playbook paid on this name. P3's 'freshest data first' led to the Nov 5 release footnote and its 'as of' guidance line. P6's decomposition of the run-in separated the company leg from the tape. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' was hard to apply without any card or panel data; Google Trends was the only demand series I could reach and it is a noisy proxy.
